title: Associativity and identity laws for ambient pullback mates
statement: Let ell be prime, E a finite extension of Q_ell, K an arbitrary base scheme and s a positive finite coefficient exponent or the whole ringed sequence site. The specified pullback comparisons and identity comparisons of [lem-sf-ambient-tensor-data-exists-unique] satisfy CompositionLaws(K,s): ordinary associativity and both unit equations, and the corresponding three exact-localization equations, for all finite-type schemes over K and all compatible scheme maps. The endpoint identifications are transports by the actual associativity and identity equalities. The definitions and hypotheses are as in [lem-sf-ambient-pullback-site-constructions].

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03EL; sites.tex 03CB; sites-cohomology.tex 06YN, 06YS, 07A4, 0G7E and 0G7D. Specialized construction and proof from the ambient coherence argument.

proof.text: The section-normalized pushComp and pushId act by restriction along the canonical base-change comparisons. Under a triple composition both maps preserve each of the three fiber-product projections. Uniqueness of the fiber product identifies them; apply the same argument to both identity cases, including transport along associativity and identity equalities of scheme maps.

Apply leftAdjointCompIso_assoc and the two identity lemmas to these right-adjoint equations and the specified module adjunctions. Their mates are exactly comp and identity by definition, so evaluating at a module proves the ordinary three clauses of CompositionLaws.

Pass the three equations to termwise complex functors. The exact localization universal property preserves compositions, identities and natural isomorphisms; its full faithfulness identifies the two natural transformations. The mapDerivedCategory factorization equations identify the localized comparators with derivedComp and derivedIdentity, including all endpoint transports.

proof_origin.place: Explicit specialization and glue for the cited adjunction, tensor and K-flat arguments; no change to the unit route.
